reviews.text: While I appreciate the attempts for bringing diversity to the Wild West, and love some of the actions scenes, this remake amuses, but mostly misfires.
reviews.author: Jana Monji

reviews.text: A solid remake with an excellent cast
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: It’s an action romp, and Denzel and company pull it off nicely.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: This is a narrow-minded, subtly mean-spirited remake.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven makes all the right noises, but misses its target.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: The action scenes are well-staged if deeply impersonal - in fact, much of the film feels rote and mechanical, less a vibrant throwback to vintage Westerns and more a marketing campaign in search of meaning.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: A safe, by-the-numbers remake of two classics designed to make money.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Could be leaner and well, maybe not meaner - I would not be surprised if it had the highest body count in a western eve r- but tighter.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: The film is little more than a few suspenseful shootouts and a bevy of humorous one-liners.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: With popcorn in hand and expectations in check, The Magnificent Seven is here for you to enjoy.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: A certain something is missing here, and it could have something to do with the questionable magnificence of some of the title characters.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: As a classic, Spaghetti-style western, it really works. The actors and the action make it an exciting journey, no matter the plot's small faults.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: It doesn't bring anything new to the formula, but it doesn't try to, and that's fine.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: What the movie lacks in edge, it mostly makes up for in energy and chemistry among the band of mercenaries, and that's just enough to give it a modest recommendation.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Over all, The Magnificent Seven is everything it was required to be. I'd say it's exactly as good as the prior incarnation, and takes enough liberties with the details to merit its own existence.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven is exactly that. If you're looking for a fun time out at the movies, you'll get that. I'm just not sure you'll remember much afterward.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: Ultimately, it's the reinvigorated Denzel Washington that makes this worthwhile, if not essential, viewing.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: On the downside, it's an uneven film. Most of the secondary characters lack depth.
reviews.author: Tish Wells

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven is an entertaining film with a mix of action, drama, and comedy.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Through successive rounds of whitewashing, one of the great works of cinema has been transformed into a bland, brainless multiplex shoot-em-up.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: Diverting action set-pieces with a mostly great cast with not nearly enough to do collectively delivers a fairly watchable rainy day outing.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven barely lives up to the 1960 film, let alone The Seven Samurai before it. But it remains an innocuous way to kill two hours, relishing in the charm of its performers and the adoration of western tropes and trappings.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: By jettisoning the nihilism that permeated its predecessors, Mag 7 basically reduced itself to a rote modern Western. That's fine for the most part, so long as no one pairs this by-the-books crowd pleaser with either of its ancestors.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Director Antoine Fuqua's ensemble-driven western The Magnificent Seven is a thrilling return to form for the genre that's more than just a remake.
reviews.author: Rick Marshall

reviews.text: This new take won't be for everyone but I found there was entertainment to be had.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: It's an orgy of beautifully choreographed death and destruction -- but not without humour.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: The reality is that while some of the subtlety of the original is lost, the bombastic nature of the story and of the characters goes a long way toward creating an engaging and extremely watchable cinematic energy.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: As an action movie, it hits all the quotas. It features booms, bullets and breasts. Just don't expect much more than that.
reviews.author: Amanda Greever

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven sticks to the cliches of the genre and doesn't disappoint. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: David Ocadiz

reviews.text: May not be magnificent, but it is still pretty fun.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: ...at least deserves to be mentioned in the same paragraph as the original, if not the same breath.
reviews.author: Zaki Hasan

reviews.text: There's nothing on the screen to suggest that this remake of The Magnificent Seven actually needed making.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: The main comparative takeaway I can give is that neither one is precisely as good as Seven Samurai, but you already knew that.
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: If you ever wanted to see a big budget remake of Blazing Saddles played entirely with a straight face, The Magnificent Seven is the movie for you.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: It captures the spirit of the original whilst not being overly reverent to it and mostly does its own thing, which is exactly what a great remake should do.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: The blandness of story and lack of intensity with action makes Fuqua's "Magnificent Seven" anything but magnificent.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: What's magnificent here is [Vincent] D'Onofrio, who has taken on a Wellesian girth that lends his isolated mountain man the air of Falstaff, albeit a Falstaff that speaks a barely intelligible language.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: Fuqua's Old West is still a bit too narratively metered and self-important to comfortably house the rambunctiously fun bronco trying to buck its philosophical rider.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: The infinitely likeable Pratt, who plays wisecracking Irish hustler Josh Faraday is definitely one of the highlights of this entertaining (yet somewhat violent) Western, offering both comic relief and guy-next door sex appeal.
reviews.author: Glynis Costin

reviews.text: This tired old reboot only cares about getting the next kill shot.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: This might be an accurate reflection of where we are now, but it's in no way a level up.
reviews.author: Sarah Manvel

reviews.text: Despite all its problems, The Magnificent Seven offers decent fun.
reviews.author: Oggs Cruz

reviews.text: This is simply a good, popcorn-crunching time at the movies.
reviews.author: Megan Basham

reviews.text: This movie is absolutely beautiful...It brings you back to that classic, Western style film. You can tell it's made today, but it feels very old school.
reviews.author: Andre Meadows

reviews.text: Let's call it "The Adequate Seven," then, since it gets the job done, yet is ultimately far short of magnificent.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: A magnificent mess.
reviews.author: David N. Butterworth

reviews.text: From the wardrobe to the sets, the whole thing pulls you in and makes you feel like you're watching a real, classic Western movie.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: While it isn't always clear why these men are risking their lives to help the people of Rose Creek, their journey, and the ultimate throwdown, makes for enjoyable viewing.
reviews.author: Rebecca Addison

reviews.text: The action, especially in the last 30 minutes, is outstanding and excellently choreographed, featuring little to no CGI. I'm also just a sucker for watching Chris Pratt act like a smart ass.
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Stranger still, in a film this progressive, this woke, that they talk about wanting their land back, without the faintest acknowledgement that they, in turn, have stolen it from Native Americans.
reviews.author: Jason Di Rosso

reviews.text: This new take on The Magnificent Seven boasts another A-list cast, but forsakes characters for bloodless, PG-13 action that entertains without resonating.
reviews.author: Kristen Lopez

reviews.text: Saddle up for a thrilling ride with this modern-day Western packed with action.
reviews.author: Reagan Gavin Rasquinha

reviews.text: There was enough potential for his character to have evolved into something truly magnificent but the chance was let slip by the director. And that, sadly, is by and large true for the whole film itself...
reviews.author: Devesh Sharma

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven isn't a masterpiece, not even close. But it is an action-packed and thoroughly enjoyable piece of commercial cinema that should keep those who like this shoot-out, stand-off, saloon-bar kind of thing highly entertained.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: ... it will probably play better to people who don't know/remember the 1960 film, but it's a solid bit of escapism.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: There's a fine line, as Sergio Leone once told me, between the operatic and the absurd, and this Seven runs roughshod over it.
reviews.author: Robert Koehler

reviews.text: It's hardly magnificent, but a solid enough date movie that provides good fun for all.
reviews.author: Jason Francis Johnson

reviews.text: This Magnificent Seven seems a bit underdeveloped character wise.
reviews.author: M. Faust

reviews.text: Magnificent? No. But still a worthwhile trip to the theater.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: This Magnificent Seven feels formulaic, but it's a solid formula.
reviews.author: Erik Henriksen

reviews.text: In the end, Fuqua has made less a magnificent seven than, at best, a slightly better than average one.
reviews.author: Dan Webster

reviews.text: Though it's an unremarkable action movie in many respects, the film has an interesting eye for symbolism that elevates it above whatever lack of freshness it may suffer from (including a lackluster script).
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: It has few standout moments and, in addition, doesn't have anything too deep or thought-provoking to say. Yet, if you simply wish to see a gun-slinging Western with some of your favorite actors, it's a least a passable couple hours at the movies.
reviews.author: David Fontana

reviews.text: This isn't just a remake, it is a straight up old-fashioned Western that stands on its own. It is very well acted and the production values are first rate. The direction by the underrated Antoine Fuqua ('Training Day') is spot on.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: An entertaining film but considering the pedigree of the two productions on which it's based, it definitely should have been much more than that. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: In rust-brown appearance as well as offhand staging of the gunfights, Faqua's 'M7' is closer to operatic Leone than choreographed Sturges ... war-weary Hawke and rousing theme by late James Horner are pluses
reviews.author: Glenn Lovell

reviews.text: The magnificence of the titular septet is barely discernible in this unwarranted update of the 1960 Western that was itself a remake of the 1954 Japanese classic Seven Samurai.
reviews.author: Rashid Irani

reviews.text: Unlike most of this year's blockbusters, his "Thoroughly Entertaining Seven" hits most of its targets.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: If you are going into The Magnificent Seven expecting a cinematic masterpiece...you will be severely disappointed. But if you want two hours of laughs, bullets, brawls, and perhaps a few tears, [it's] a serviceable distraction.
reviews.author: Jacqueline Coley

reviews.text: The end result is a paint-by-numbers Western that will scratch that itch, but should have done a better job of justifying its existence.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: With so many personalities and characters, there's little time for any standout performances... or a standout film. That said: it isn't bad, either.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: As things build toward the long, bloody and by-the-numbers (if ably staged) showdown, it's hard not to mourn for the film this could have been, considering the assemblage of talent.
reviews.author: John Wenzel

reviews.text: It is not, by and large, a very inspired film, though sometimes it gets there in spurts.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: A more than rollicking-enough cinematic ride.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: ...a seriously misguided and misbegotten remake.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Washington is still the star of the film, but he stands out by underplaying while his peers go over the top. He provides a calm center as Fuqua stages some expert gunplay and equine action.
reviews.author: Dan Lybarger

reviews.text: It's respectful of the past, while it blazes into the future of a genre that is as American as covered wagons.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: This unoriginal reboot reveals Washington and Fuqua to be hacks as they take on a formerly great genre, the Western...This craven, doubled-down remake reduces America's difficult history to a series of violent, affectless, and inept set-pieces.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: The action is fine, but the movie lacks the grandeur that makes this genre special: The landscapes are unattractively photographed, evidence that this 'Western' -- a few New Mexico scenes aside -- mostly was shot in Louisiana, for tax-credit purposes.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: The big problem with the film is that it has no real reason to exist...The characters are lifeless, the pace is slow, the villain is a wimp.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Not nearly as magnificent as the originals it is based on, this Denzel Washington western vehicle still has its moments even if there is too much gunplay and not enough character development.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: As Gene Wilder tributes go, it's not bad.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: Outside of being a tad overproduced, it stands on its own perfectly well.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: Although it doesn't have the emotional pull of the 1960 John Sturges classic, this modernisation of The Magnificent Seven is still a rip-roaring action western.
reviews.author: Richard James Havis

reviews.text: With all of the superficial style but none of the rousing spirit of the source material, Fuqua's film is less The Magnificent Seven, more The Perfunctory Few.
reviews.author: Roe McDermott

reviews.text: After a disappointing blockbuster season, The Magnificent Seven was the popcorn flick that we've been waiting for
reviews.author: Yasmin Kleinbart

reviews.text: If you're looking for a comparison between the most popular remake and Kurosawa's masterpiece, better see one of those two, because you won't find anything that gets close to the best of the genre. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: It's a pretty authentic reimagining of a classic story, and as remakes go, it's not half bad.
reviews.author: Sarah Griffin

reviews.text: It is easy to cheer for the underdogs and hiss at the villains, and The Magnificent Seven makes no bones about playing to those easy sentiments for rousing good-vs-evil theatrics.
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: An unnecessary film but with will make you have a good time. The audacity to redo an already excellent film doesn't bother much. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Abuín

reviews.text: Much more than a remake, an outstanding film that surpasses its predecessor. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Díaz Reyes

reviews.text: Made with polish and buoyed by a rousing score, this remake is worth seeing on the big screen, largely due to the thrilling, climactic finale when bullets, arrows and knives find their marks.
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: Antoine Fuqua's new remake of 'The Magnificent Seven' is not a great Western, but it's a damn fine one - and it's got a great Western hero at its center, which is just as important.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: This latest remake is far from perfect but in a time when westerns are few and far between, it provides a nice throwback to a forgotten genre.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: An old-school western, full of good guys, bad guys, gunplay and grit.
reviews.author: Tom Glasson

reviews.text: Rootin-tootin' self-aware of its grandeur. Drawls out the build-ups to the mega-climax and refuses to tie-up the terse, macho dialogue to taut, whip-smart action sequences.
reviews.author: Brian Gibson

reviews.text: A copy of a copy in all respects.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: [It] has a pleasing full-on embrace of things a western must have: tobacco spitting, gun twirling, trick riding, men bursting out of saloon doors, men bursting out of saloon windows, men just bursting.
reviews.author: Russell Baillie

reviews.text: This most satisfying, testosterone-fuelled shoot-'em-up is great fun, with pleasing work from the whole cast.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: An agreeable remake, not bad for an Antoine Fuqua flick, if ultimately an unmemorable movie.
reviews.author: Aaron Yap

reviews.text: Westerns have enjoyed a small renaissance over the last decade. The Magnificent Seven may not be the best of them, but it's a respectable effort with a game cast helmed by a justifiably confident director.
reviews.author: Alex Doenau

reviews.text: This is perhaps damning it with faint praise, but Fuqua's Magnificent Seven will always easily be the third best version of this story.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven is better than the film that it's remaking in many ways; but when you're talking about how it stands up with the original source material of Seven Samurai, it's already been eclipsed by the incredible 13 Assassins.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: Most of the time, it feels like Fuqua is just ticking the boxes of the genre conventions, which would be fine if all he was trying to do is make a run-of-the-mill Western TV movie. But this is The Magnificent Seven for god's sake.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: ...a straightforward tale of good guys and bad guys built on gunfights, machismo, and double barrelled toughness.
reviews.author: Erin Free

reviews.text: Relatively entertaining.
reviews.author: Marija Djurovic

reviews.text: It is spectacular, has lots of great lines -- most of which go to Pratt -- and the performances are all solid, although Sarsgaard isn't great as the baddie.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: Denzel Washington, as we've come to expect from this masterful and unfussy screen actor, carries the entire film by sheer force of personality.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: The main issue about this film is that tries too much to show a world where good people are clearly different from bad people, where honor overcomes cowardice, and where kindness and loyalty overpowers the thirst for money. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Fernando Galván

reviews.text: A western on autopilot.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: Those hoping that The Magnificent Seven would be a return to a classic Western set during the Old West will be disappointed. Those looking for a great Western, with a modern-day setting, should seek out Hell or High Water.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: Fuqua skirts anything remotely interesting from a thematic standpoint, opting instead for a by-the-books modern re-imagining of the genre. Modern as in violent.
reviews.author: Eric Melin

reviews.text: A well-crafted and patient remake that takes the time to develop its characters before the large-scale violence ensues.
reviews.author: John Hanlon

reviews.text: The sight of Denzel twirling his six-guns and shooting from the hip will be more than enough, for many, to make The Magnificent Seven a rousing success.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven is an awkward milestone in Hollywood's ongoing and urgent conversation about representation.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Awash in chintzy CGI, the film has a sickly avocado sheen to it, as if it was color-corrected in post-production to look like a can of Bud Lime.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: The 1960 movie has always been a favorite of mine....remakes never usually match up, and that is the case here.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: I wasn't expecting much of this remake, other than to determine if it should have been remade in the first place. And the answer is a clear "no" -- not the greatest use of $95,000,000.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Even a phalanx of good actors can't save this-less than-Magnificent Seven...
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: Very clever and fingernail-biting excitement.
reviews.author: Diana Saenger

reviews.text: Washington and Pratt show true grit in this movie, but a lack of character depth makes it entertaining only for those who love violence.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: There's even a woman this time. She's a match for any of the men, and might have been included among their number had it not been necessary for her to shed tears at one point, and to serve the guys dinner at another.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: There are shoot-outs galore and the story trots along but what should be rousing entertainment falls rather flat.
reviews.author: Henry Fitzherbert

reviews.text: It's certainly watchable stuff, but if Fuqua wasn't going to do anything new with the material, you rather wonder what was the point?
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: The most rousing moment in The Magnificent Seven comes after the action has already concluded, when the credits roll to the emphatic accompaniment of Elmer Bernstein's iconic 1960 score.
reviews.author: Christopher Orr

reviews.text: ...an old-time western with a modern sensibility. Unlike all too many remakes, it fully justifies its existence
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: If there's a pulse emanating from a single member of Fuqua's high-falutin' cast it's undetectable.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Antoine Fuqua's action-filled, shoot-em-up remake, supplying a spectacular barrage of bullets.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Humorless, rote, clichéd, and entirely unsurprising. Antoine Fuqua attempts to recapture old Hollywood magic - and fails - rather than create his own.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: An undistinguished remake of the 1960 iconic lighthearted macho western starring Yul Brynner.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: All the low angles looking up at our heroes makes them look heroic, and the wide shot of all seven walking down the street feels special.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Dull, predictable, and basic in every sense of the word, The Magnificent Seven is a devastating blow to the western genre and yet is about the standard as far as remakes go.
reviews.author: Chris Sawin

reviews.text: Traces of real history are hard to spot in Fuqua's Western, but there isn't much evidence of a real Western, either. You sense that an entire genre, far from being revitalized, is being plundered for handy tips.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: If you can get past the places where the new movie fails to match the original, it's a Western that shoots straight.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: Things couldn't possibly seem more wheezy and tired than they do when played out in a narrative framework that had already run its course by the time Yul Brynner and Steve McQueen took it on in 1960.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: Already getting tired and sick to see this kind of productions that are also unnecessary and becoming obsolete. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Israel Acosta Aroche

reviews.text: A film with an endless gunshot salad in the middle of it resulting in an exhausting experience. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Bermejo

reviews.text: A movie with a chaotic approach to action scenes, making it sink into the indecipherable. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jordi Costa

reviews.text: There is a lot to like about 'The Magnificent Seven,' which never tires to be anything more than an entertaining, spirited movie.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: An action movie as chaotic as fun. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: A solid and entertaining reinterpretation of a classic story. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jesús Chavarria

reviews.text: The movie never seems to click as it should. The ensemble never quite matches the prickly rapport of the original cast (or, for that matter, the cast of The Seven Samurai, the Akira Kurosawa film that inspired the 1960 western).
reviews.author: Randall King

reviews.text: Maybe it's impossible to make classic Westerns any more. We'd probably need to unlearn lots of stuff we think we know first. This isn't one, but it would certainly fill some time on a long flight, or on your iPad in the middle of a sleepless night.
reviews.author: Adam Sweeting

reviews.text: If body count is what you go to Westerns for, by all means drift into this one's corral.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven (2016) isn't going to eclipse its predecessors but it is, nonetheless, an immensely entertaining and heartfelt action-western experience.
reviews.author: Ben Kendrick

reviews.text: Without Washington the picture would wither into dust. With him on board it proves, well, perfectly adequate.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: While you know where the storyline is going, what keeps you interested are the well-choreographed action set pieces and the jokes.
reviews.author: Theresa Smith

reviews.text: The new Magnificent Seven, though seriously flawed in one or two aspects, is actually a very successful remake and a really solid film in its own right.
reviews.author: Ilan Preskovsky

reviews.text: The film's resounding theme about self sacrifice is sure to put a bit more jangle in your spurs.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: D'Onofrio bursts from a bush looking like Grizzly Adams, if Grizzly Adams had eaten Orson Welles for breakfast.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: This one was always more crowd-pleaser than poetry, but it contains simple, strong messages, codes of honor that still ring true.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: ... generates a decent camaraderie among its culturally diverse ensemble cast, yet rather than exploring new territory in the Old West, it too often treads familiar ground amid all the bullets and bravado.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Admittedly, the cinematography is stunning, but the story is mediocre and the dialogue borderlines on corny.
reviews.author: Whitney Scott Bain

reviews.text: If you've already seen Hell or High Water and the itching and scratching of waiting for the galactic gun-slinging of Rogue One and Guardians II is still proving too much, give this a go.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: Holds up as an action-packed western thrill ride that serves up a phenomenal climactic showdown.
reviews.author: Mark Ellis

reviews.text: Much like Suicide Squad, The Magnificent Seven is a ensemble piece about misfits that races through Act One to skip to a prolonged Act Three... I'm not mad at it...
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven has no real substance, meaning, or depth. It simply is what it is: a breezy Western adventure with a bunch of name actors. On that level, it works.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The talkative script keeps reiterating what we're seeing: "Dang it, I'm good!" Pratt says, feeling good about himself once again. "I sense we are bonding," we hear, as the seven men bond, masticating cheroots and cigars they don't seem to want to smoke.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: As summer fare, it's bloody entertainment that, if nothing else, gives young comic book superhero audiences a throwback taste of that endangered Hollywood species -- the Western.
reviews.author: Barry Paris

reviews.text: Antoine Fuqua's The Magnificent Seven won't make longtime fans forget the 1960 Sturges original, but it is a tense and dramatic western that feels like a perfect reflection of a violent 2016.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: To tackle such an updating without fully loaded guns is not a wise thing.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: A worthy tribute to the original 1960 classic, and it's a great ride for fans of action or westerns.
reviews.author: Kristian Harloff

reviews.text: Westerns may be a nostalgic genre, few and far between these days, but it doesn't have to be outdated when filmed, as Fuqua does, through a 21st-century lens.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven is a thoroughly satisfying, well-executed modern-day Western.
reviews.author: David Blaustein

reviews.text: Even with its fair share of shortcomings the entertainment factor remains high enough throughout to make giving it a shot exceedingly worthwhile.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: No, this "Magnificent Seven" doesn't reinvent the wagon wheel, but it's not supposed to.
reviews.author: Anders Wright

reviews.text: A far cry from the 1960 Sturges film, never mind the Kurosawa classic. But better than expected. Washington and Pratt make a fun, if unlikely duo.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: The emotion and heart of the movie gets lost in an all the action. But the stars make it kind of entertaining at times, and if all you're looking for is a violent shoot em' up Western with a high body count, it fits the bill.
reviews.author: Neil Rosen

reviews.text: Fuqua isn't interested in the contemporary Western. His Magnificent Seven is a throwback to those decades-old films that informed him as an impressionable and young filmmaker. But to live in history invites comparisons to what was.
reviews.author: Kirk Baird

reviews.text: The idea of a team of outlaws recruited to protect the innocent has been replayed so often in so many genres (science fiction and war action, most notably) that [The Magnificent Seven] feels less like a remake and more like a repeat.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Politically bizarre, the film is competent but routine.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: Certainly not magnificent, but decent enough for what it's trying to do and be. (Full Content Review for Parents - Violence, Sexual Content, Profanity, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: It's not great - it's no 'The Magnificent Seven' - but it'll satisfy any varmint hungry for some Old West justice.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven ends up being a bit too predictable to reach its full potential, but the fun the cast clearly had making it allows the movie to be an enjoyable ride while it lasts.
reviews.author: Terri Schwartz

reviews.text: The scenery and cinematography are eye-boggling. New Mexico is the go-to location for primal sunsets, majestically pillared cliffs and a light that leads to eternity. When your eyes stray to the battles and shoot-outs, they're pretty good too.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: It's certainly fun, and a spectacle to behold in IMAX, but if you're going to remake the 1960 classic, which starred Yul Brynner and Steve McQueen, you need to make a cinematic cavalry charge into the territory of modern sensibilities.
reviews.author: Kate Muir

reviews.text: The movie cannot escape its been-there-shot-that vibe.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: Fuqua's made two clean piles separating good and evil, and in doing so, he's thrown away the film's point.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Those bread-and-butter scenes feel fumbled or half-hearted.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Chris Pratt is better off playing in his own 'Galaxy' than starring in an oater.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: This edition isn't as hokey as the original but has trade-offs in its action packed finale where gunslingers defy credibility sharpshooting from horseback and firing Colt .45s with both hands.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Hokey but often very funny, "The Magnificent Seven (2016)" succeeds as an action film but fails to be about anything significant.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: ...a comic book film set in the west, with stock characters equally given to violence and wisecracks...
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: Not quite as good as the old Magnificent Seven and certainly not as good as Seven Samurai, but ... if you're into this sort of thing, you'll like it just fine.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: The word Magnificent might be a bit boastful.
reviews.author: Willie Waffle

reviews.text: In aspiring to present itself as a diverting mainstream action film, this only ever manages to be a diverting mainstream action film. Magnificence never enters the equation.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Fuqua's rendition delivers plenty of quick-draw action and is respectful to the source material; it just can't challenge the epic romanticism or magnificence of the 60s classic.
reviews.author: Jeremy Aspinall

reviews.text: The final showdown is actionpacked and well staged but we never really care about any of the characters, making this Magnificent Seven merely adequate.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: "Magnificent" is pushing it, but "The Magnificent Seven" - the latest spin on the classic outlaw tale - comes in guns blazing, sweeps the town and gets the job done.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The film rests upon the more-than-worthy shoulders of Denzel Washington - who brings his trademark strut, iconic slouch, and a cocked gun paired with that legendary cocked head.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: This is the way to remake. Look to the lineage of The Magnificent Seven for real evolution; a variety of voices behind and in front of the camera.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Antoine Fuqua uses a hammer and anvil approach to a story that has more subtlety than he gives it.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven isn't. But it's a western and I love westerns so it gets enough points to recommend.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: While it might not launch a Western cinematic resurgence, The Magnificent Seven gives the genre a much needed shot in the arm. Say hello to the fall's first big blockbuster.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: This version of "The Magnificent Seven" offers a viciousness and hardscrabble harshness earlier incarnations lacked.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Everyone seems a little too aware that they are Making A Western For A Modern Audience rather than throwing themselves headfirst into making a Western for a modern audience.
reviews.author: Joe Gross

reviews.text: Inevitably, the movie spends a lot of time getting ready for the climactic showdown. But it's so chaotic and protracted as to lose much of its punch.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: The re-imaging of 'Seven' is not the most magnificent western we'll ever see, but it's certainly no by-the-book remake, either.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Fuqua Helms Magnificent Muddle.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The film is OK, it's the name that's all wrong.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: As with most Westerns, the focus is on the final showdown and, readers, this is ace. Thrilling, bloody, gruesome, really well shot. I loved it.
reviews.author: Jamie East

reviews.text: It's efficient but soulless and relies on well-choreographed action sequences to maintain the attention rather than any effort to flesh out the characters led by Denzel Washington's monosyllabic lawman Sam Chisholm.
reviews.author: Tim Evans

reviews.text: Why? Does the world really need a third iteration of this story? And one without the outstanding cast and iconic performances of its predecessor? And one with an imbecilic final battle which drags on long enough to kill every extra in Hollywood?
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: In a summer filled with remakes, reboots, sequels and superheroes that have more often than not disappointed, Fuqua has delivered a classic style of filmmaking that crowd-pleases without blowing you completely away.
reviews.author: Rob Carnevale

reviews.text: The sheer brilliance of these latter scenes justify this new version of an old favourite and shows us just why Westerns are still worth making.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: There may not be any surprises, and only a whiff of thematic interest in the corporate greed element, but the film is still rip-roaringly entertaining.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Explosive action and a good cast make Antoine Fuqua's exciting reboot a western worth seeing.
reviews.author: Roger Tennis

reviews.text: If the sight of Denzel Washington, guns blazing and saddled up for his first western, doesn't get your pulse racing, read elsewhere.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: You could do worse than putting it all in the capable hands of Denzel Washington, with some help from Chris Pratt.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Witty crosstalk should be one of the pleasures to be had in a men-on-a-mission movie like this one, but there's not enough of it.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: I'm sorely disappointed.
reviews.author: Tirdad Derakhshani

reviews.text: In their few scenes together, Hawke and Washington, so vital in Fuqua's Training Day, hold the screen with sheer chemistry, and perhaps a bit of history. If only this film had known what to do with the richness of its raw material.
reviews.author: Michelle Orange

reviews.text: [Fuqua] deals in constant commotion, repetitive confrontations, stylized formations, laser-like scowls (or, in the case of one young woman in town, a fixed glower), and violence that's both aestheticized and anesthetized.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: The film has some superficial style, and the action sequences are put together competently enough, but there's little or no sense of jeopardy, of danger threatening people you might really care about.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: It all builds to a climactic battle in and around the town that feels almost apocalyptic in its level of violence and destruction.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Long on violence and short on story, character development, motivation, and all the things that make any kind of violence satisfying to watch.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: The result here won't erase the memory of Sturges' classic, but it does pay due homage to it.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: You shouldn't be surprised to learn that Denzel Washington as a badass gunslinger is amazingly cool, and enough to make The Magnificent Seven an enjoyable if overlong experience.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: A very efficient and entertaining film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: A very entertaining movie that will make you have a great time. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven is a cast and a title in search of a movie. Not only did they not find one, I'm not certain they even looked.
reviews.author: Will Leitch

reviews.text: This entertaining and handsome-looking version of "The Magnificent Seven" is very much tailored to his star, right down to Washington's real-life history as a preacher's son.
reviews.author: Lou Lumenick

reviews.text: If there's a compelling reason to remake The Magnificent Seven, it can't be found in the 2016 version, a loud, cluttered, and generally disappointing production.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Over all, this is a rousing, albeit sometimes cheesy, action-packed Western.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: There isn't anything particularly magnificent about the Seven or the movie itself, even though it makes for a fun, summery popcorn movie in the early days of fall.
reviews.author: Christopher Lawrence

reviews.text: All the efforts to modernize the Western feel half-baked at best, like slapping one coat of paint on a crumbling house.
reviews.author: Lauren Chval

reviews.text: An ethnically diverse cast and snappy action scenes make for an entertaining update of the 1960 classic.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Antoine Fuqua hardly tightens the reins on his adaptation, which stretches 90 minutes of entertainment across a 132-minute frame. Too bad the gang didn't recruit an eighth member who was an expert at editing.
reviews.author: Jon Niccum

reviews.text: "The Magnificent Seven" is fine as far as it goes, but - especially when the familiar strains of the 1960 theme song begin wafting over the final scenes - one can't help feeling that it should have gone much further.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: The new Magnificent Seven also suffers from flabby, leisurely editing, but it does offer something Sturges' Western doesn't: the most inept strategist in the history of American Western villains.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: Director Antoine Fuqua proves that the western is far from dead with this rousing update of John Sturges's 1960 classic (itself adapted from Akira Kurosawa's The Seven Samurai).
reviews.author: Andrea Gronvall

reviews.text: This new edition of the much-told story is...a perfectly watchable couple of hours [but] it certainly doesn't match the standard Sturges and his charismatic cast...set nearly sixty years ago.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: After assembling a cast as good as this and then squandering them, Fuqua may have won the battle while losing the war.
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: Overlong and often struggling to balance action and comedy, The Magnificent Seven is an uneven effort with some sensational action.
reviews.author: Bill Clark

reviews.text: Usually Washington's charisma is enough to see him through a problematic genre exercise. Here, I suspect, we have a movie that'll split audiences between responses of "not bad" and "not good enough."
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: If the best westerns have always been, in some way, studies of contemporary manhood, it's worrisome to think about what this Magnificent Seven says about men today.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: You may check your watch occasionally, but we don't get many old-fashioned Westerns these days.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: It's a fun movie, a nicely made Western in which bad guys get to be good guys sometimes. Maybe that should be enough, but you can't help wanting more.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Only when there's an opportunity to blow things up does Fuqua seem fully engaged.
reviews.author: Calvin Wilson

reviews.text: A sense of lethargy hangs uneasily over the lumbering new version of "The Magnificent Seven."
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: He looks so powerful, so beautiful, so right that you may find yourself wondering how we had a black president for seven full years before Washington got to play the lead in a Western.
reviews.author: Alan Scherstuhl

reviews.text: Denzel Washington and Chris Pratt make an entertaining pair, but The Magnificent Seven doesn't bring anything new to the genre.
reviews.author: Scott Chitwood

reviews.text: It's not exactly magnificent, but it's a slick and entertaining take on a familiar tale that's bursting with personality.
reviews.author: Jason Zingale

reviews.text: While there's enjoyment to be had, there's not a whit of surprise. You come to an Antoine Fuqua movie not to be taken somewhere new but to tour an old neighborhood with tough-guy professionalism.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Brings the cowboy past into focus with the Hollywood present.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: This director does have a flair for rhythmically intense set-pieces, and his whole film justifies its existence when the bullets start flying.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Call it the mighty entertaining "Seven," and you'll be right.
reviews.author: Lawrence Toppman

reviews.text: Fuqua has watched his John Ford, evident in the sweeping mountain vistas that use every inch of the screen, and his Sergio Leone, represented by the squinty tension that fills the air before every showdown.
reviews.author: Chris Vognar

reviews.text: Occasional one-liners and nihilistic truisms are all that the cast has to work with, and they don't give much in the way of characterization.
reviews.author: Ignatiy Vishnevetsky

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven, as derivative as it may be, makes for a decent couple of hours wasted.
reviews.author: Aisha Harris

reviews.text: The new movie is as moth-eaten as the serapes strewn through the 1960 film, but there's no denying the appeal of the image of Mr. Washington riding a horse, shooting a Colt and leading a posse of vigilantes to save a mostly white Western town.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Count this one as a guilty pleasure.
reviews.author: Soren Andersen

reviews.text: There's plenty to reject about this joyless effort, which always seems to be at odds with its natural charisma, weirdly downplaying excitement and feisty camaraderie as Fuqua continues to work through his anger issues.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: This new version of The Magnificent Seven works thanks to its first class cast, great action sequences and an impressive directing job by Antoine Fuqua. The Magnificent Seven is solid entertainment. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Fuqua's remake is an entertaining neowestern influenced by Kurosawa's Seven Samurai since the opening credits. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Marañón

reviews.text: [Delivers] action-packed fun throughout, culminating in a brilliantly staged show-down that will leave you feeling thrilled.
reviews.author: Amy West

reviews.text: Almost wholly inessential.
reviews.author: Mike McCahill

reviews.text: Washington, who plays Chisolm as a confident but thoughtful leader who uses his brains as much as his guns, and Hawke, as the troubled PTSD-struck Robicheaux, are especially impressive.
reviews.author: Laura DeMarco

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven is an unapologetic crowd pleaser, filled with daring anti-heroes, thrilling shootouts, and bloody gallows humor.
reviews.author: J.R. Kinnard

reviews.text: The trick of the 1960 version is that it carries itself lightly... The new Magnificent Seven is the worst of both worlds: Completely substance-free, yet heavier than Vincent D'Onofrio's beard.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: The title is about one-seventh right.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: After nearly a year of hype, The Magnificent Seven has arrived and proven itself to be another entertaining if underwhelming remake of a well-regarded flick.
reviews.author: Edward Johnson-Ott

reviews.text: As with The Equalizer, Washington's commanding presence helps elevate what otherwise might be ordinary.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: Its sepia-tinted bones are weathered, but spit-shined real nice, sporting an all-star cast and a gold mine of studio production value.
reviews.author: Blake Goble

reviews.text: The unofficial cowboys and outlaws played by Pratt in Guardians of the Galaxy or Denzel in any number of Tony Scott movies have more pizazz than this bunch.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: As solid as he is crafting the look of a good Western, Fuqua fails to build much momentum, or engagement with the characters.
reviews.author: Peter Hartlaub

reviews.text: If you're looking for something different from the 1960 original - or the movie that was based on, the 1954 classic Seven Samurai - it's best to mosey elsewhere, pilgrim.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: The remake of the 1960 classic Western moseys along at the pace of a long-in-the-tooth horse.
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: As remakes go, Fuqua's version is perfectly entertaining in terms of action and character. But it is unlikely to replace the original in anyone's affections.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: "The Magnificent Seven" is a Western. Maybe that's good enough.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: Silly, solid entertainment: multiplex fun by numbers.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: The Wild, Wild West revisited as an ethnically-diverse fantasy land Hollywood has never imagined before!
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: A film that make us recover the greatness of what cinema is, how it is filmed, how was enjoyed before a big screen.[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcos Gandía

reviews.text: As well made as it is, it's still got that title, which is both blessing and curse in this case, as it does too little to distinguish itself from the 1960 classic.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: It should be noted that The Magnificent Seven is more like a very cool two and a half, counting Ethan Hawke's wonderfully named Goodnight Robicheaux, a former Confederate marksman whose PTSD is a brief drag on the action.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: Fantastic cast chemistry and the raw, leading-man star power of Denzel Washington provides a mighty lift when needed.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: As usual, Washington is cool as a cuke, Pratt could play this role in his sleep, and Hawke is moving from hipster to hipflask swigger with grace.
reviews.author: Matt Glasby

reviews.text: As passably entertaining as the film is, it never surrenders to the abandon of its action and as such never feels like it shifts out of first gear.
reviews.author: Jake Cole

reviews.text: The John Ford cliches clang against the Sergio Leone sloppy seconds with the hollow ring of a church bell.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: Most of these characters barely register as human at all for the first two-thirds of the film, in which they are virtually indestructible.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: Strong direction from the always versatile Antoine Fuqua and game performances from the entire cast make The Magnificent Seven a total blast from start to finish.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: Oh wait, so you decided to wait until September to give us a halfway decent summer action movie? Thanks, I think.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: Perfectly acceptable escapism.
reviews.author: Stephen Mayne

reviews.text: It's a really solid, really fun classical shoot 'em up.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: They say each generation deserves their own version of a classic story, and Magnificent 7 is the version this generation deserves: polished but still remarkably unremarkable.
reviews.author: Ali Gray

reviews.text: An entertaining film but nothing else. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Arturo Aguilar

reviews.text: Not quite magnificent but certainly Fuqua's best since Training Day and a rare remake that actually delivers. Yee-haw!
reviews.author: Jamie Graham

reviews.text: Fuqua's remake is a complacent film and nothing else. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Benjamín Harguindey

reviews.text: There's a fine line between a slowburn and dull, and this Magnificent Seven frequently finds itself on the wrong side.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: Slick but forgettable, Fuqua's suicide squad is a macho posse movie that could use a jab of fun. It's The Magnificent Seven, but the "magnificent" is silent.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: A vehicle for wall-to-wall action, and an unambiguously fond farewell to the Obama years.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: It's awfully pleasant to watch Denzel Washington, Chris Pratt, Vincent D'Onofrio and Ethan Hawke (among others) saddle up and ride out against an evil coal baron (Peter Sarsgaard) who's trying to drive some settlers off their land.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: The western genre is defined by its gritty and grimy aesthetic. Fuqua crafts his world with too little tumbleweed and too much Hollywood sheen.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: Doesn't find enough interesting new wrinkles on the old formula.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: It's a reminder that movies don't just entertain. They can inform. They can smuggle in new ideas, and set new expectations. If that's the kind of thing that can be achieved by remaking classic old movies, I'm all for it.
reviews.author: Bryan Bishop

reviews.text: An exercise in genre that has echoes of the John Sturges and Akira Kurosawa versions, but little of the charm of the former and none of the depth of the latter.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Maybe some classics should just stay classics.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven is Western "dumb fun," which works just fine with proper expectations.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: The world needs the Three Amigos! treatment as much as they do Seven Samurai -- just don't expect anything more.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Magnificent? Not quite, but a more accurate title -- say, The Perfectly Average Seven -- doesn't pack the marketing punch needed to sell the latest retelling of a very familiar story.
reviews.author: Sean O'Connell

reviews.text: A bigger, but dumber and louder remake.
reviews.author: Kevin Jagernauth

reviews.text: It's a rousing good time at the movies.
reviews.author: Liz Braun

reviews.text: Fuqua's Magnificent Seven is Fast & Furious on horses -- The Wild Bunch for people who will never bother to see The Wild Bunch
reviews.author: Jen Yamato

reviews.text: 'The Magnificent Seven' seems to be happiest when it's mindless action spectacle, but it's disappointing that Fuqua doesn't ask for anything more.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: Too traditional for its own good, Fuqua makes an entertaining underdog tale, but not one that justifies revisiting a classic.
reviews.author: Stefan Pape

reviews.text: A fun reboot of the classic ensemble western. Denzel Washington is at his best as the gun-slinging leader.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: What Fuqua's Magnificent Seven lacks in originality it makes up for in personality, with his Training Day and The Equalizer compadre Denzel Washington earning his oats as an ensemble leader in his first western.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Nothing particularly original or fresh has been injected into this competently made, violent but uningratiating remake of the star-studded John Sturges Western, which itself was a redo of Akira Kurosawa's imperishable 1954 classic, Seven Samurai.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: A fun and surprisingly fresh Western that takes aim at Donald Trump's America.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Such an unapologetic throwback to old-fashioned western heroism that 'de-visionist' is the only descriptor that reasonably comes to mind. It's an uncomplicated, handsome, exciting action-adventure.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: Satisfying, action-packed remake of the 1960 western classic, with an appealing ensemble cast led by Denzel Washington.
reviews.author: Kevin Lally

reviews.text: A solid script and cast and a fantastic ending battle helps Antoine Fuqua's first Western stand out despite being rather conventional.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: The Magnificent Seven is what Suicide Squad should have been.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: There's certainly enough verve, and love for the genre, to help one get past its trouble spots, but you can't help feeling the mercenary thinking behind rehashing this mercenary yarn.
reviews.author: Robert Abele

synopsis: Looking to mine for gold, greedy industrialist Bartholomew Bogue seizes control of the Old West town of Rose Creek. With their lives in jeopardy, Emma Cullen and other desperate residents turn to bounty hunter Sam Chisolm (Denzel Washington) for help. Chisolm recruits an eclectic group of gunslingers to take on Bogue and his ruthless henchmen. With a deadly showdown on the horizon, the seven mercenaries soon find themselves fighting for more than just money once the bullets start to fly.
